ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
On January 22, 2015, a magnitude 4.2 earthquake occurred in the Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. It is known that the propagation speeds of the P-wave and S-wave near the surface during the earthquake are $9.1\mathrm{km/s}$ and $3.7\mathrm{km/s}$, respectively. At the epicenter observation station, the time difference between the arrival of the P-wave and S-wave from the source was recorded as $5.4\mathrm{s}$.

1. Find the distance from this observation station to the seismic source.
2. What the observatory first observed was vertical oscillation or horizontal shaking?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: On January 22, 2015, a magnitude 4.2 earthquake occurred in the Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. It is known that the propagation speeds of the P-wave and S-wave near the surface during the earthquake are 9.1 km/s and 3.7 km/s, respectively. At the epicenter observation station, the time difference between the arrival of the P-wave and S-wave from the source was recorded as 5.4 s. 1. Find the distance from this observation station to the seismic source. 2. What the observatory first observed was vertical oscillation or horizontal shaking?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: 34 km Vertical oscillation (up and down vibration)
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Let the source-to-station distance be d. The P-wave speed is v_P = 9.1 km/s and the S-wave speed is v_S = 3.7 km/s. Since P-waves are faster, the arrival-time difference is Δt = t_S - t_P = 5.4 s. Using t_P = d/v_P and t_S = d/v_S gives Δt = d(1/v_S - 1/v_P). Therefore d = 5.4 / (1/3.7 - 1/9.1) km = 33.7 km, which rounds to 34 km. The first motion observed is due to the faster P-wave; in this context P-waves correspond to vertical up-and-down oscillation, while S-waves arrive later and cause horizontal shaking.
